Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

theory noun

an idea that explains something

also a theory, my theory is, hypothesis

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.25: haec nova et ignōta ratiō

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a theory, an explanation, a system of ideas

Lewis & Short: “a theory, doctrine, or system based upon reason”. What the theory holds follows in an accusative and infinitive (Cic. Rep. 1.25).

Examples

  • erat enim tum haec nova et ignōta ratiō, sōlem lūnae oppositū solēre dēficere

    for this was then a new and unknown theory: that the sun is eclipsed when the moon is set against itCic. Rep. 1.25

Other words

  • conjectūra, conjectūrae f. — a conjecture, a theory that cannot be proved

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.22.1: nē nihil conjectūrā aberrem

    See guess.

See also theory, idea, guess, reason.

SourcesLewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: conjectura
